sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:1-22: imports UnifiedTradingAccount/MockBroker; createUTA constructs UTA directly and flush advances fake timers for constructor-started _connect
entries.currentBehavior: createUTA chooses a MockBroker, calls new UnifiedTradingAccount(broker), and flush() advances fake timers by zero because construction launches _connect without awaiting it.
entries.problem: The fixture makes timer flushing and constructor fire-and-forget part of the observable lifecycle. A test can see an object before its connection admission is known, and no durable startup phase is represented.
preservedBehavior: Keep test isolation and MockBroker as the deterministic broker fixture.
Intentionally remove the assertion that zero-time timer flushing is the lifecycle contract; readiness must be awaited through a typed coordinator.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:24-35: fake-timer test expects automatic connect to healthy, Date lastSuccessAt, recovering false
entries.currentBehavior: After createUTA and flush, the test reads health=healthy, requires lastSuccessAt to be a Date, and recovering=false.
entries.problem: Healthy currently conflates transport/account readiness with a mutable Date snapshot and is observed only after an unstructured timer flush. It does not say which capability was proven or whether journal recovery completed.
preservedBehavior: Preserve successful MockBroker connection and the source timestamp observation, but encode it as typed Instant/provenance rather than requiring a JavaScript Date.
Preserve the distinction between public data reach and funded private-read reach; neither implies global RuntimeHealth.Ready by itself.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:37-48: MockBroker failMode makes init throw; test expects offline/recovering/lastError and closes
entries.currentBehavior: One init failure leaves health offline, recovering true, and lastError containing the simulated exception; close is awaited.
entries.problem: Error text and booleans are the only failure evidence. The test cannot distinguish unavailable credentials, transport handshake closure, disabled configuration, or a journal that failed before broker acquisition.
preservedBehavior: Preserve offline/recovering semantics for an unavailable broker.
Replace contains(lastError) with stable typed code plus diagnostic evidence; do not promise exact message wording.
openQuestions: Exact native error-code mapping from each adapter to permanent versus transient remains unproven; until a versioned adapter declaration exists, unclassified BrokerError stays transient Unavailable with recovery and never Disabled.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:50-67: first init fails, five-second fake time advances, recovery becomes healthy/non-recovering
entries.currentBehavior: After an initial failure, advancing 5_000ms runs the first recovery attempt and the account becomes healthy with recovering=false.
entries.problem: Recovery timing is encoded by setTimeout and only tests in-memory state. It is not durable work, has no owner/epoch, and cannot classify transactions that were executing while the connection was down.
preservedBehavior: Preserve the source-compatible 5-second first retry and eventual healthy result after a transient failure.
Use an explicit 5s base, factor 2 and 5-minute cap for the connection policy; this policy is not a dispatch retry policy and cannot be applied to Unknown mutations.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:69-91: failMode=100 and fake time advances 5s,10s,20s; offline/recovering stays true
entries.currentBehavior: Recovery attempts occur at 5s, 10s, and 20s and retain offline/recovering when init keeps failing; close cancels the loop.
entries.problem: The test proves an exponential sequence but does not prevent recovery timers from duplicating, does not fence stale attempts, and does not connect backoff to durable job state. Most importantly, this schedule cannot be reused for mutation retries after Unknown.
preservedBehavior: Preserve capped exponential reconnect intent and close cleanup.
Intentionally prohibit using this schedule as a generic retry helper for order sends; Unknown remains reconciliation-only.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:93-110: failMode=2, initial and first recovery fail, second at 15s succeeds
entries.currentBehavior: The initial attempt and first recovery fail; after another 10_000ms (total 15s) the second recovery succeeds and health is healthy.
entries.problem: Only the happy endpoint is asserted; there is no evidence that the first failed generation was closed, that the second probe is not concurrent, or that pending durable work is reclassified during the interval.
preservedBehavior: Preserve eventual recovery after two transient failures.
Add explicit proof that recovery success does not imply transaction success.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:112-127: after healthy connect, three getAccount failures expected to produce degraded
entries.currentBehavior: Three consecutive getAccount rejections move the health string from healthy to degraded.
entries.problem: Failure counting is mutable and method outcomes are reduced to a threshold. A transport-alive/private-read failure needs capability-specific degradation, otherwise callers may treat an account as wholly unavailable or still safe for writes.
preservedBehavior: Preserve the source-compatible 3-failure degraded boundary and 6-failure offline boundary as versioned defaults; thresholds are evidence policy, not authorization.
Do not permit stale or failed account facts to satisfy execution preconditions merely because a threshold counter changed.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:129-141: six getAccount failures expected offline and recovering=true
entries.currentBehavior: Six consecutive account failures set offline and start automatic recovery; close is called.
entries.problem: The threshold moves from degraded to full offline but does not specify whether existing broker transport is closed, how pending jobs are fenced, or what callers can still read.
preservedBehavior: Preserve the source-compatible six-failure offline/fail-fast boundary, but express it as a typed account capability outcome rather than an independent recovering flag.
Existing dispatch intents are durable and are never deleted just because the connection is offline.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:143-159: six failures drive offline, 5s recovery restores healthy/recovering false
entries.currentBehavior: After six failed getAccount calls the test advances 5s; a broker success yields healthy and recovering=false.
entries.problem: Recovery success is inferred from one timed probe but the test does not inspect the fresh observation, connection generation, durable leases, or other accounts.
preservedBehavior: Preserve successful runtime recovery and clearing recovering.
Require a fresh typed account/connection observation rather than a timer event alone.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:161-175: four failures produce degraded, next successful getAccount resets health/counter
entries.currentBehavior: Four failed calls leave degraded; the next successful getAccount changes health to healthy and consecutiveFailures=0.
entries.problem: A success reset is unconditional and does not verify freshness, scope, or whether the read is the capability needed for the caller. A successful market-clock call should not necessarily make account-read capability healthy.
preservedBehavior: Preserve successful recovery of healthy state and failure-counter reset for the same operation.
Correct the broader “any success means healthy” assumption by scoping the reset to capability.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:177-188: getAccount and getPositions failures share count; getMarketClock success yields healthy
entries.currentBehavior: Failures across getAccount/getPositions increment one shared counter; a successful getMarketClock returns health healthy.
entries.problem: The shared counter demonstrates cross-method reachability but overstates what market-clock success proves: account/position data may remain unavailable while clock is reachable.
preservedBehavior: Preserve the source observation that failures from multiple broker methods contribute common transport evidence, but no longer use one shared counter as the authorization state.
Preserve data-tier health when its required public capability is reachable; funded account health still requires its private account capabilities.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:191-207: six failures then getAccount expected offline/reconnecting fail-fast
entries.currentBehavior: Once six failures trigger recovery, a later getAccount rejects with text “offline and reconnecting” without another broker call.
entries.problem: The fail-fast behavior is correct safety intent but string-matched and implemented inside one mutable account object. There is no explicit indication whether a caller may read a stale projection or queue a durable command.
preservedBehavior: Preserve fail-fast/no-broker-call safety.
Replace regex message expectation with a typed failure and retry deadline.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:209-222: after offline, stage/commit then push rejects with offline text
entries.currentBehavior: The test stages and commits a BUY locally, then push rejects while broker is offline; close follows.
entries.problem: Push is still a direct mutation path after local Git commit. It does not create a durable transaction/dispatch intent before checking reachability, so a process crash cannot distinguish prepared work from an attempted remote mutation.
preservedBehavior: Preserve the source refusal of push while offline and zero broker calls on that path.
Preserve funded readOnly ability to retain/review a draft, but never promote it to PreparedPlan/Approved/Queued or dispatch.
Preserve the unsent ReturnToAgent review branch as durable review/outbox state with explicit retain/rearm/revise/discard semantics and zero broker dispatch.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:224-241: stage and commit succeed offline, result.staged=true and prepared=true without broker contact
entries.currentBehavior: Offline status does not prevent local staging or commit; commit reports prepared=true without contacting the broker.
entries.problem: This proves proposal preparation can be local, but current Git state is process/in-memory/file-backed and is not a durable approval transaction. `prepared=true` has no digest, revision, before-image, expiry, or recovery evidence.
preservedBehavior: Preserve offline local staging and funded readOnly reviewability as non-executable DraftReview, including descriptive preparation analysis when facts are supplied.
Replace the source in-memory `prepared=true` claim with explicit revision/fact/digest states; no offline executable prepare is inferred from connectivity absence.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/__test__/uta-health.spec.ts:244-258: permanently failing broker leaves recovering true; close then timer cancellation makes recovering false
entries.currentBehavior: Close cancels the recovery timeout and sets recovering=false after a permanently failing initial connection.
entries.problem: The test checks a local timer flag but not Scope finalization, worker interruption, broker close, durable job quiescence, or late callback fencing. Clearing recovering can be mistaken for successful recovery.
preservedBehavior: Preserve timer cancellation and no post-close recovery.
Change recovering=false interpretation to Closed status, distinct from successful Healthy.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/index.ts:1-2: barrel imports ./contract-ext.js for a global IBKR Contract extension
entries.currentBehavior: The trading barrel imports ./contract-ext.js; contract-ext.ts and protocol contract-ext.ts contain only TypeScript module augmentations/imports, while UnifiedTradingAccount explicitly reads/writes contract.aliceId at runtime.
entries.problem: The barrel has an unnecessary compatibility import and public SDK types can leak into domain imports; the source does not show prototype mutation or runtime installation of aliceId.
preservedBehavior: Preserve aliceId/canonical identity semantics where the protocol still exposes them.
Remove global side effect and require explicit mapping at adapter boundaries.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/index.ts:4-6: barrel exports UnifiedTradingAccount and stage parameter types
entries.currentBehavior: The barrel exposes UnifiedTradingAccount as a class plus UnifiedTradingAccountOptions and stage-place/modify/close parameter types.
entries.problem: Public import establishes the legacy class and stage API as a runtime execution authority, allowing routes/tools to bypass transaction-kernel preparation and durable receipts.
preservedBehavior: Preserve named place/modify/close intent and read-only draft review through protocol commands.
Remove the class export rather than retaining a runtime alias that can reach legacy stage/push methods.

entries.currentBehavior: UTAManager is re-exported as the manager entry point from the trading barrel.
entries.problem: The export makes a map-backed manager that owns lifecycle, broker construction, aggregation, persistence and tools look like the domain’s canonical authority, contrary to durable account/application ownership.
preservedBehavior: Preserve account listing/query behavior at protocol level.
Remove runtime class export and avoid read facade that still owns mutations.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/index.ts:10-15: barrel reexports UTASummary, AggregatedEquity, ContractSearchResult, SnapshotHooks from manager
entries.currentBehavior: The manager barrel reexports three response types and SnapshotHooks alongside the manager class.
entries.problem: These types appear canonical but are coupled to a mutable manager and expose legacy aggregation/snapshot semantics; SnapshotHooks are callbacks rather than durable events.
preservedBehavior: Preserve summary fields needed by current UI.
Remove callback type as execution hook and model trigger as durable event.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/index.ts:17-24: barrel exports IBroker, Position, PlaceOrderResult, OpenOrder and notes against eager SDK imports
entries.currentBehavior: The barrel exports the generic broker interface and execution/read model types from brokers/index.
entries.problem: IBroker’s broad methods allow action/result mismatches and PlaceOrderResult implies remote success/possibly fill without action-specific acknowledgement/observation. Exporting it from a domain barrel spreads adapter types.
preservedBehavior: Preserve read/query concepts represented by Position/OpenOrder after provider-specific decoding.
Preserve provider-native read/write details through exact adapter extensions rather than forcing every provider to implement one set of actions.
Preserve the source fact that a broad IBroker/PlaceOrderResult surface currently exists and that generic result mapping is unsafe.
Delete generic write interface/PlaceOrderResult authority rather than claiming unsupported action coverage.
openQuestions: Native idempotency, completeness, and atomic protection remain per-provider evidence for each declared controlled-effect leaf; no abstraction resolves them.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/index.ts:25-30: barrel exports AccountInfo, Quote, MarketClock, AccountCapabilities, TpSlParams
entries.currentBehavior: The barrel makes heterogeneous broker account/quote/clock/capability/TP-SL records broadly importable.
entries.problem: One generic surface erases contextual capability: account balances, market observations, and order attachment parameters have different provenance, scope and uncertainty. Consumers can mistake a native record for a validated domain value.
preservedBehavior: Preserve account/quote/clock meanings and TP/SL where broker supports them.
Do not silently broaden native capabilities just because a generic type was exported.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/index.ts:31-33: barrel reexports createBroker async concrete factory
entries.currentBehavior: Consumers can import createBroker from the domain barrel; it resolves preset/engine and constructs concrete brokers asynchronously.
entries.problem: The domain barrel becomes a factory locator and config/SDK boundary, bypassing composition Layers, credential ownership and scoped resource lifetimes.
preservedBehavior: Preserve preset-to-engine selection semantics and optional pack behavior.
Remove createBroker as public runtime API rather than wrapping it in a manager.
openQuestions: Installed pack availability and pack-specific native idempotency/late-observation guarantees still require pack manifest/conformance evidence; missing or unverified evidence keeps the scoped account capability unavailable and forbids dispatch.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/index.ts:35-58: barrel exports TradingGit and complete staging/commit/push/sync type surface
entries.currentBehavior: The barrel exposes TradingGit plus operation, commit, push, sync, GitState and export types as the public trading workflow.
entries.problem: Git-shaped classes/types become execution and persistence authority; commit hashes can be mistaken for transaction identities, and file-backed state can bypass atomic journal writer.
preservedBehavior: Preserve human-readable history requirement and action order.
Remove Git push as mutation authority and do not preserve file fallback as hidden durability.

entries.currentBehavior: The barrel exports snapshot creation/scheduling/storage/build APIs and their file-backed types from domain/trading.
entries.problem: Snapshot implementation and schedule are visible as domain services even though files are rebuildable projections; timer/store ownership can compete with JournalStore and execute before recovery.
preservedBehavior: Preserve snapshot history/read endpoints and periodic capture intent.
Move ownership and trigger away from Git callbacks/file store.

entries.currentBehavior: The barrel exposes mutable guard registration/resolution and built-in guard types from the legacy path.
entries.problem: Guards are reachable as generic runtime registry entries and can read broker/Git state or return strings; permissive unknown registry types and dispatch-time IO undermine deterministic preparation.
preservedBehavior: Preserve built-in risk intent (cooldown, max position, whitelist).
Remove string errors, mutable global registry and dispatch-time reads; unsupported guard types are explicit failures.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/keyless-data-sources.ts:3-7: LABELS maps closed binance/okx/bybit enum values to labels
entries.currentBehavior: LABELS is a total Record over KeylessDataSource and is used to generate display labels.
entries.problem: Presentation labels live next to account identity construction, encouraging a string/config value to become a runtime account without venue metadata or capability context.
preservedBehavior: Preserve exact labels where UI depends on them.
Move labels out of transaction-kernel/domain identity semantics.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/keyless-data-sources.ts:9-15: comments state keyless UTAs are not persisted to accounts.json and require explicit trading.json opt-in
entries.currentBehavior: The policy documents opt-in public-data accounts, excludes them from accounts.json, and avoids unsolicited exchange connections.

preservedBehavior: Preserve explicit opt-in and no unsolicited public-exchange connection.
Preserve the source non-persistence in accounts.json while retaining a durable, non-funded registration projection for restart/reconciliation.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/keyless-data-sources.ts:17-23: buildKeylessDataUTAs deduplicates source array in insertion order and filters generated ids in existingIds
entries.currentBehavior: The function uses Set to preserve first occurrence, skips `${ex}-readonly` collisions, and returns one config per remaining source.
entries.problem: Dedup/collision is deterministic but uses raw strings and a caller-provided Set. It cannot distinguish an authoritative funded account, stale registry row, disabled account, or incompatible same-id registration.
preservedBehavior: Preserve insertion-order dedup and avoidance of shadowing a user account.
Strengthen collision behavior: same string is not enough to silently treat unlike account kinds as identical.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/keyless-data-sources.ts:24-36: maps selected source to UTAConfig with generated id/label, ccxt-custom preset, booleans keyless/readOnly/asVendor/editable
entries.currentBehavior: Each selected source becomes enabled ccxt-custom config with empty guards, keyless/readOnly true, asVendor true, editable false and exchange in presetConfig.
entries.problem: Boolean flags and untyped presetConfig can be contradictory or bypassed. The config lacks venue/jurisdiction/session metadata and offers no type-level distinction between historical data and executable account actions.
preservedBehavior: Preserve generated labels, enabled/public-data intent, vendor discovery participation.
Do not preserve `readOnly` as the only mutation barrier; enforce at application/kernel.
openQuestions: Concrete per-venue jurisdiction, session calendar, and public endpoint metadata still require adapter catalog evidence; missing fields keep DataSourceRegistration Unavailable and do not permit guessed defaults.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/keyless-data-uta.spec.ts:1-5: test documentation says optional binance/okx/bybit read-only, no key, pure construction/no network
entries.currentBehavior: The spec is explicitly construction-only: it imports factory/builder and promises no network; no runtime capability or plan refusal is exercised.
entries.problem: Construction can prove no eager network call but cannot prove scoped public connection, absence of credential use, or that transaction admission rejects data-only accounts.
preservedBehavior: Preserve no-network pure-construction intent for this unit.
Add, rather than infer, runtime security evidence in a separate integration case.
openQuestions: No remote public-venue run in this unit establishes historical endpoint reach or freshness; until scoped adapter evidence exists, historical capability remains Unavailable/Unknown and construction-only tests cannot promote it.

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/keyless-data-uta.spec.ts:24-27: selected binance/okx produce ordered generated ids

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/uta-manager.spec.ts:231-249: getContractDetails returns details for known account and null for unknown; asserts native contract fields

sourceEvidence: services/uta/src/domain/trading/uta-manager.ts:1-21: manager imports Decimal, IBKR types, createBroker/preset, CCXT tools, UnifiedTradingAccount, Git persistence, config, EventLog/ToolCenter, FxService and contract-ext while declaring lifecycle/query ownership
entries.currentBehavior: UTAManager sits under domain/trading but imports concrete SDK, broker factory, file persistence, Alice services and side-effect extension to own lifecycle and aggregation.
